name: async
whatItDemonstrates: Loading search results asynchronously while typing (simulated Top-100-movie search), with fully custom Status content covering pending, error, empty, and result-count states.
stateManaged: controlled — useState wrapping the input value wired via value/onValueChange; additional useState for results and error, React.useTransition for pending state, and a useRef holding an AbortController for stale-request cancellation.
nonTrivialInteractions: filter={null} disables built-in filtering so the rendered items are entirely owned by the async fetch results
onValueChange fires a simulated fetch with random 100–600ms delay, aborts the previous request via AbortController, and skips applying results if aborted
React.useTransition marks fetch updates as pending and drives a spinner in the custom Status content
Autocomplete.useFilter()'s contains matcher is reused manually inside the async search to match both movie title and year
Popup sets aria-busy while pending; Portal is hidden={!status} so nothing renders until there is status content

name: auto-highlight
whatItDemonstrates: The first matching item is automatically highlighted as the user types via the autoHighlight prop on Root.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; the component manages input value, open state, filtering, and highlight internally.
nonTrivialInteractions: autoHighlight (boolean) highlights the first filtered item without any keyboard interaction
List uses a render-prop child over the tags array; items style the highlight via data-highlighted with a ::before overlay
Empty renders a 'No tags found.' message when the query matches nothing

name: command-palette
whatItDemonstrates: A command palette: the autocomplete input filters grouped app/command suggestions rendered inline inside a Dialog, and activating an item 'runs' the command by closing the dialog.
stateManaged: controlled — Dialog open state via useState(open/setOpen) wired to Dialog.Root open/onOpenChange; the Autocomplete.Root itself is forced open with a static open prop and no open/close state of its own.
nonTrivialInteractions: Autocomplete is rendered with inline + static open inside Dialog.Popup — no Autocomplete.Portal/Positioner/Popup at all
autoHighlight='always' combined with keepHighlight keeps an item permanently highlighted, including during mouse interaction
Item onClick closes the Dialog (command activation); a hidden sr-only Dialog.Close inside the palette provides an escape affordance, and a footer documents that Enter activates the highlighted item
List render-prop iterates groups; each Group receives its own items array and renders GroupLabel plus a Collection render-prop for the items
Accessibility wiring: aria-label on the Input and aria-describedby pointing at a visually hidden element describing the Enter shortcut; Dialog.Popup carries aria-label='Command palette'
ScrollArea wraps the list region with a custom scrollbar

name: fuzzy-matching
whatItDemonstrates: Replacing the default filter with a fuzzy matcher (match-sorter over title/description/category) and highlighting the matched query substring inside each item using the Value render prop.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; filtering is delegated to the custom filter function.
nonTrivialInteractions: Custom filter function using matchSorter (with per-key rankings CONTAINS / WORD_STARTS_WITH) replaces the locale-aware default filtering
Autocomplete.Item wraps an Autocomplete.Value render prop exposing the current input value, used by a regex-based highlightText helper that wraps matches in <mark>
The Empty message embeds <Autocomplete.Value /> to echo the unmatched query back to the user
itemToStringValue maps object items to their title for matching/serialization

name: grid
whatItDemonstrates: An emoji picker: a button-triggered popup with grid layout (5-column rows via Autocomplete.Row) that inserts the selected emoji into an external message input at the caret.
stateManaged: controlled — useState for popup open (pickerOpen) wired to open/onOpenChange; useState for the search value (searchValue) wired to value/onValueChange; plus useState + useRef for the external text input (textValue) the emoji is inserted into.
nonTrivialInteractions: grid prop enables two-dimensional (per-column) keyboard navigation across the 5-column rows
Items are chunked into rows of 5 with a chunkArray helper and each row is wrapped in an Autocomplete.Row inside per-category Groups with GroupLabel
onValueChange ignores updates whose details.reason is 'item-press' so selecting an emoji does not overwrite the search text
onOpenChangeComplete clears the search value after the picker closes
Item onClick inserts the emoji at the external input's caret (setSelectionRange), refocuses the external input, and closes the picker via setPickerOpen(false)

name: grouped
whatItDemonstrates: Organizing filtered options into labeled groups (Type / Component) using Group and GroupLabel with items supplied per group.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; the component manages input value, open state, and filtering internally.
nonTrivialInteractions: List render-prop iterates an array of group objects ({ value, items }) and renders one Autocomplete.Group per group with its items prop
Autocomplete.Collection render-prop renders the individual items inside each group
Group labels are rendered via Autocomplete.GroupLabel from the group's value property
Empty renders a 'No tags found.' message when the query matches nothing

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: The baseline autocomplete: typing in the input filters a flat tag list shown in an anchored popup, with an empty-state message.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; the component manages input value, open state, and filtering internally.
nonTrivialInteractions: List uses a render-prop child over the tags array; items carry value={tag} object values
Items style the highlight via data-highlighted with a ::before overlay
Empty renders a 'No tags found.' message when the query matches nothing
Popup width tracks the input via --anchor-width CSS variables

name: inline
whatItDemonstrates: Inline completion via mode='both': the input is autofilled with the highlighted suggestion while the popup list filters as you type.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; the component manages input value, open state, filtering, and highlight internally.
nonTrivialInteractions: mode='both' provides list suggestions plus inline completion of the input value from the highlighted item
No Empty part is used — instead the Positioner is hidden when the list is empty (data-empty:hidden in Tailwind) and the List collapses its padding via data-empty
List uses a render-prop child over the tags array

name: limit
whatItDemonstrates: Capping the visible results with the limit prop while a Status line tells the user how many results are hidden and to refine their query.
stateManaged: controlled — useState wrapping the input value wired via value/onValueChange; a useMemo recomputes the total match count from that value to derive the hidden count.
nonTrivialInteractions: limit={8} truncates how many filtered items render in the List

The demo mirrors the component's internal filtering by calling Autocomplete.useFilter({ sensitivity: 'base' }) and running contains over the full dataset in a useMemo to compute how many matches exceed the limit
Autocomplete.Status renders a 'Hiding N results' hint only when moreCount > 0
Empty message echoes the current input value

name: virtualized
whatItDemonstrates: Rendering a 10,000-item dataset efficiently with @tanstack/react-virtual, including keeping the highlighted item in view during keyboard navigation.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state for the autocomplete itself; windowing state lives inside useVirtualizer, surfaced to the Root via a virtualizerRef (useImperativeHandle).
nonTrivialInteractions: virtualized prop on Root tells the component items are windowed; Item receives an explicit index prop plus aria-setsize/aria-posinset to keep the listbox ARIA contract correct
Autocomplete.useFilteredItems called inside the child list component returns the internally filtered array that feeds the virtualizer's count
onItemHighlighted scrolls the virtualizer (scrollToIndex in a queueMicrotask) whenever highlight moves for reason 'none' or keyboard navigation hits the first/last item
Item refs are wired to virtualizer.measureElement for dynamic size measurement; the scroller div uses a --total-size CSS variable to cap its height
openOnInputClick opens the popup when the input is clicked, not just when typing
